title: Flash Droughts: Why Speed, Not Scarcity, Is the New Systemic Risk
key_claim: Flash droughts are a distinct policy category whose speed compresses warning windows from months to weeks and outpaces existing triggers for insurance payouts, relief delivery and political mobilisation; they have increased in frequency and intensity since the 1950s and are projected to rise further.
notes: Primary framing anchor — argues this is a new systemic-risk category, not a slower-onset drought variant.

title: Global Seasonal Climate Update for April-May-June 2026
key_claim: Multi-model consensus shows a rapid transition into El Nino territory by May 2026 with several models suggesting strong El Nino as early as June/July; widespread above-normal global land surface temperatures forecast for AMJ 2026; strong tropical Pacific signal with broad below-normal rainfall over the Maritime Continent and the eastern Indian Ocean.
notes: Quantification anchor for global ENSO transition driving 2026 drought-onset risk.

title: National Current Conditions
key_claim: As of 13 May 2026, 51.35% of the United States and Puerto Rico and 61.47% of the Lower 48 are in drought; hot, dry April produced considerable drought expansion in the lower Mississippi Valley, Southeast and Mid-Atlantic, with significant impacts on soil moisture, streamflows and reservoirs.

publisher: World Economic Forum (African Risk Capacity contributed article)
title: How disaster risk financing can anchor Africa's development and strengthen its resilience
key_claim: African Risk Capacity sovereign parametric model has provided over $1 billion in coverage to member states and disbursed more than $350 million in insurance claims; February 2026 high-level dialogue with IFAD and WFP called for continental expansion of parametric insurance.
notes: Anchors the scaling of sovereign parametric drought insurance and pre-arranged finance.

publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization / Food Security Information Network (FSIN)
title: Global Report on Food Crises 2026 (GRFC)
key_claim: Acute hunger has doubled over the past decade with two famines declared last year for the first time in the report's history; climate variability and risks to food markets likely to sustain or worsen conditions in many countries in 2026; Sahel faces a difficult pastoral lean season due to drought.
notes: Authoritative multilateral anchor for the human-impact dimension.

title: Aon 2026 Climate and Catastrophe Insight: increasing climate risk from flood and drought
key_claim: Drought attributed around $13 billion in economic losses in 2025; flooding exceeded $42 billion in 2025; in 2025 the US recorded 14 separate 24-hour rainfall events consistent with a 1-in-1,000-year flood level; pluvial flood risk in the US could rise by ~12% under a medium-emissions and ~19% under a high-emissions scenario by mid-century.
notes: Reinsurance-industry anchor for re-pricing of secondary-peril losses.

title: East Africa drought triggers parametric payouts to farmers worth $9 million
key_claim: More than 70,000 farmers across the Horn of Africa received payouts under the World Bank-financed DRIVE parametric insurance scheme; 17,734 pastoralists in Somalia received payments after satellite-based monitoring confirmed Deyr-season (Oct-Dec 2025) rainfall far below normal.
notes: Specific event anchor for operational parametric insurance triggers in 2026.
